title: Guided Onboarding Checklist — Copy Drafts (Hosted API, Phase 1)
content:
Doc purpose
- Working copy drafts for the Console “Guided onboarding” checklist (Hosted API scope).
- Intended to be used by Design/Console eng/Docs. Expect iteration.
- Notes include alternatives + decisions after reviews.

Audience + tone
- Audience: self-serve engineers evaluating/implementing Redwood API for the first time.
- Tone: confident, direct, minimal fluff. Prefer verbs + concrete outcomes.
- Avoid jargon where possible; if used (e.g., “streaming”, “rate limit”), add a short clarifier.
- Consistency rules:
  - Use “project” (not “workspace”) unless Console explicitly uses org. If org is required, say “org (team)”.
  - Use “API key” consistently; when needed: “Test key” vs “Prod key”.
  - Prefer “make your first request” vs “call the API”.
  - Prefer “Usage dashboard” (Console nav) vs “analytics”.

Checklist structure proposal (Phase 1)
- We’re grouping steps into 2 sections in the UI:
  1) Get set up (fast path to first success)
  2) First production launch (minimum safeguards + observability)

Validation constraints (what the UI can auto-check)
- Auto-validated (expected in Phase 1):
  - API key created (server signal)
  - First successful request (gateway logs/metrics; may have a lag)
  - First streaming session (server signal; edge cases around disconnect)
  - Visited Usage dashboard (client event)
  - Prod-mode key created (Console key type)
- Not auto-validated (Phase 1):
  - “Retries/timeouts implemented” (we can only educate + link)
  - “Safe rollout” (guidance + link)
  - “Guardrails” beyond docs

Open copy question
- Do we explicitly mention “this may take ~1–2 minutes to update” for validated steps?
  - UX suggestion (Kenji): subtle helper text only on validated steps, not globally.
  - PM suggestion (Nikhil): add it only when we detect the user completed the action but the signal hasn’t arrived yet.

—
STEP 0 (entry state): Checklist card title + description

Title options
A) “Guided onboarding”
B) “Get to production”
C) “Launch checklist”

Description options
A) “Complete these steps to make your first request, then get ready for your first production launch.”
B) “Follow the steps below to integrate the Redwood API with confidence.”
C) “Start here: set up a key, run a request, then add the minimum production safeguards.”

Decision (2026-01-22 design sync)
- Use Title A (“Guided onboarding”).
- Use Description A with small edit: replace “make” with “send”.

Final (current)
- Title: Guided onboarding
- Description: “Complete these steps to send your first request, then get ready for your first production launch.”

CTA (top-level)
- Optional: “View quickstart” (deep link)
  - Concern (Docs): multiple SDKs; link should go to “Choose your SDK” landing page, not a single language.

—
STEP 1: Create an API key

Goal
- User creates any API key for the project (initially test key is fine).

Step title options
A) “Create an API key”
B) “Create your first API key”
C) “Create a test API key”

Description options
A) “Create a key to authenticate requests to the Redwood API.”
B) “You’ll use this key in your SDK/client. You can create a production key later.”
C) “Keys are scoped to a project. Store it somewhere safe—Redwood won’t show it again.”

CTA label options
A) “Create key”
B) “Go to API keys”
C) “Create API key”

Helper / warning text options (small, under description)
A) “Tip: Use a test key while you’re prototyping.”
B) “Keep keys out of client-side apps. Use a server.”

Edge-case/error copy
- If the user has no permission:
  - “You don’t have permission to create API keys. Ask a project admin for access.”

Decision notes
- 2026-01-16 (Support input): must preempt 401 confusion from wrong key type.
  - Add sentence that test keys may not work in prod environments if restrictions exist.
- 2026-01-24 (Design review): keep it short; avoid “store it somewhere safe” lecture in main copy.

Current draft
- Title: “Create an API key”
- Description: “Create a key to authenticate requests to the Redwood API.”
- Helper: “Tip: Use a test key while you prototype.”
- CTA: “Go to API keys”

—
STEP 2: Install an SDK (or call the REST API)

Goal
- Provide a clear next action without forcing a language choice in the Console.

Step title options
A) “Install an SDK”
B) “Install an SDK (recommended)”
C) “Set up your client”

Description options
A) “Use one of our SDKs for streaming, retries, and typed errors.”
B) “Choose Python, TypeScript, or Go. Prefer REST if you’re integrating from another language.”
C) “Get a working client set up locally in under 5 minutes.”

CTA options
A) “Choose your SDK” (docs landing)
B) “View SDKs”
C) “See quickstart”

Decision notes
- 2026-01-21 (Docs IA): CTA should go to a stable landing page that lists languages.
- 2026-01-27 (Monica/SDK): don’t promise “typed errors” everywhere unless parity confirmed.

Current draft
- Title: “Install an SDK (recommended)”
- Description: “Use an SDK for streaming and consistent retry behavior. Or call the REST API directly.”
- CTA: “Choose your SDK”

—
STEP 3: Send your first request

Goal
- User gets a successful response from Hosted API.
- Validation: “first_successful_request” (may lag).

Step title options
A) “Send your first request”
B) “Run a hello-world request”
C) “Make a successful API call”

Description options
A) “Send a simple chat completion and confirm you get a 200 response.”
B) “Copy/paste a snippet and verify the response in your terminal.”
C) “We’ll automatically check this step after your first successful request.”

CTA options
A) “View first request example”
B) “Open quickstart: first request”
C) “See example code”

Validation helper text (only when relevant)
- “Checking for a successful request… this can take up to ~2 minutes.”

Error-state copy (when we detect repeated 401/429)
- 401 hint: “Getting 401? Double-check you’re using an active API key for this project.”
- 429 hint: “Getting 429? You may be hitting rate limits. See quota guidance.” (deep link)

Decision notes
- 2026-01-18 (PM): avoid “chat completion” terminology if we might rename endpoints; use “generate” / “chat” generically.
- 2026-01-22 (Design): don’t say “200”; say “successful response”.

Current draft
- Title: “Send your first request”
- Description: “Send a simple request and confirm you get a successful response.”
- CTA: “Open quickstart: first request”

—
STEP 4: Try streaming

Goal
- Users learn streaming and avoid “why is it slow?” perception.
- Validation: “first_streaming_session” signal.

Title options
A) “Try streaming responses”
B) “Enable streaming”
C) “Stream tokens (recommended)”

Description options
A) “Stream tokens to reduce time-to-first-token and improve UX.”
B) “Learn how to handle partial responses and disconnects safely.”
C) “Streaming is recommended for interactive apps and long outputs.”

CTA options
A) “View streaming example”
B) “Open streaming guide”
C) “See streaming snippet”

Troubleshooting microcopy (if streaming disconnect common)
- “If the stream disconnects, retry with the same request ID when possible.”
- NOTE: confirm request ID guidance is accurate across SDKs.

Decision notes
- 2026-01-27 (SDK parity): keep retry/request-id advice out of main copy until we’re sure it’s consistent.

Current draft
- Title: “Try streaming responses”
- Description: “Stream tokens to reduce time-to-first-token and improve UX.”
- CTA: “Open streaming guide”

—
STEP 5: Structured output or tool calling (pick one)

Goal
- Introduce at least one “production-ish” capability that reduces downstream parsing errors.
- Reality: UI likely cannot enforce “pick one” in Phase 1; might be informational.

Title options
A) “Return structured output”
B) “Use structured output or tool calling”
C) “Add structured output (recommended)”

Description options
A) “Get JSON you can validate instead of parsing free-form text.”
B) “Use tool calling when the model needs to fetch data or take actions.”
C) “Structured output reduces brittle parsing and makes failures easier to debug.”

CTA options
A) “Structured output guide”
B) “Tool calling guide”
C) “See examples” (landing page that links both)

Decision notes
- 2026-01-15 (Tessa): don’t force a fork in the checklist UI in v1.
- 2026-01-23 (Docs): create a combined landing page later; short-term link to structured output as default.

Current draft (v1)
- Title: “Return structured output”
- Description: “Get JSON you can validate instead of parsing free-form text.”
- CTA: “Structured output guide”

—
SECTION BREAK: First production launch

Section title options
A) “First production launch”
B) “Go live safely”
C) “Production readiness”

Section description options
A) “Minimum safeguards we recommend before shipping to users.”
B) “Add reliability, observability, and a rollback plan.”
C) “Before you ship: harden retries, set quotas, and enable monitoring.”

Decision (Product thread 2026-01-21)
- Use A + A. Align language with PM-483.

Current draft
- Section title: “First production launch”
- Section description: “Minimum safeguards we recommend before shipping to users.”

—
STEP 6: Create a production API key

Goal
- Make the distinction explicit to reduce 401s due to wrong environment.
- Validation: “prod_key_created”.

Title options
A) “Create a production API key”
B) “Create a prod key”
C) “Switch to a production key”

Description options
A) “Use a production key for real user traffic. Keep test keys for development.”
B) “Production keys should be stored in your secret manager and only used server-side.”
C) “We’ll label this key as ‘prod’ in the Console.”

CTA options
A) “Create prod key”
B) “Go to API keys”

Decision notes
- 2026-01-19 (Support): strongly prefer the word “production” over “prod” in UI copy.
- 2026-01-24 (Security reviewer Marcus, via notes): avoid implying Redwood enforces secret manager usage; phrase as recommendation.

Current draft
- Title: “Create a production API key”
- Description: “Use a production key for real user traffic. Keep test keys for development.”
- CTA: “Go to API keys”

—
STEP 7: Add timeouts + retries

Goal
- Reduce first-week production incidents and support load.
- Not auto-validated in v1.

Title options
A) “Add timeouts and retries”
B) “Handle errors with retries”
C) “Make requests resilient”

Description options
A) “Set request timeouts and retry transient failures with backoff.”
B) “Handle 429s and timeouts without breaking your app.”
C) “Use SDK defaults or copy a tested retry wrapper.”

CTA options
A) “Retries & timeouts guide”
B) “See recommended retry config”
C) “View error handling examples”

Microcopy (optional)
- “Tip: Start with SDK defaults and adjust based on latency SLOs.”

Decision notes
- 2026-01-28 (Fireflies beta check-in summary): users want this earlier, but PM prefers production section to keep “time to first success” short.

Current draft
- Title: “Add timeouts and retries”
- Description: “Set request timeouts and retry transient failures with backoff.”
- CTA: “View error handling examples”

—
STEP 8: Review rate limits + quotas

Goal
- Reduce 429 confusion and set expectations.
- Partial validation: can validate “visited quota page” in future; for now link.

Title options
A) “Review rate limits and quotas”
B) “Understand rate limits”
C) “Set quotas for your project”

Description options
A) “Know what triggers 429s and how to handle them.”
B) “Confirm your project limits before onboarding real traffic.”
C) “Set safeguards to prevent surprise usage.”

CTA options
A) “Open quotas” (Console deep link)
B) “Rate limits guide” (docs)

Decision notes
- 2026-01-20 (Marissa): if Console has a quotas page, CTA should go there (better activation).
- 2026-01-25 (Support): must explicitly mention 429.

Current draft
- Title: “Review rate limits and quotas”
- Description: “Know what triggers 429s and how to handle them.”
- CTA: “Open quotas”

—
STEP 9: Check the Usage dashboard

Goal
- Encourage early observability + cost visibility.
- Validation: “visited_usage_dashboard”.

Title options
A) “Check usage and latency”
B) “Open the Usage dashboard”
C) “View usage analytics”

Description options
A) “Track tokens, latency, and errors so you can debug and control cost.”
B) “Confirm requests are flowing and check your token usage.”
C) “Use this to spot spikes and 429s early.”

CTA options
A) “Open Usage dashboard”
B) “View Usage”

Decision notes
- 2026-01-22 (Design): align title with nav label. Prefer B.

Current draft
- Title: “Open the Usage dashboard”
- Description: “Track tokens, latency, and errors so you can debug and control cost.”
- CTA: “Open Usage dashboard”

—
STEP 10: Plan a safe rollout (canary + fallback)

Goal
- Provide a minimum bar: canary, rollback, and model/version pinning guidance.
- Not auto-validated.

Title options
A) “Plan a safe rollout”
B) “Roll out safely”
C) “Add a rollback plan”

Description options
A) “Start with a small percentage of traffic and have a rollback ready.”
B) “Pin a model version, then use canary testing to catch regressions.”
C) “Use fallbacks if your app needs high availability.”

CTA options
A) “Rollouts guide”
B) “First production launch doc”

Decision notes
- 2026-01-21 (PM): link to the canonical “First production launch” doc (single page) so we don’t fragment guidance.
- 2026-01-26 (Docs): ensure the doc page title matches the step language to reduce confusion.

Current draft
- Title: “Plan a safe rollout”
- Description: “Start with a small percentage of traffic and have a rollback ready.”
- CTA: “First production launch doc”

—
Global UI copy (misc)

Step states
- Not started: “Not started” / “Start”
- In progress: “In progress” / “Continue”
- Completed: “Completed”

Auto-validation status (small helper text)
- Option A: “We’ll mark this complete automatically.”
- Option B: “Marked complete after we detect it in your project.”
- Option C: “This may take a minute to update.”

Current recommendation
- Use Option B only on steps we validate, and only as subtle helper text (not in the main description).

Empty-state / first-run banner copy
- Banner title options:
  A) “Welcome—let’s ship your first request”
  B) “Welcome to Redwood Inference”
  C) “Start building with the Redwood API”
- Banner body options:
  A) “Create an API key, run a quick request, then follow the production checklist.”
  B) “Use the checklist to set up authentication, streaming, and production safeguards.”

Decision (2026-01-28)
- Title A, Body A.

—
Review log / decisions (high signal)
- 2026-01-15 (Tessa/Kenji): Avoid forked steps (tool calling vs structured output). Keep checklist linear in v1.
- 2026-01-16 (Support/Dev Patel): Explicitly mention 429 in rate-limit step and reduce “mystery failures” language.
- 2026-01-19 (Support/Priya): Use “production” not “prod” in user-facing copy.
- 2026-01-21 (PM Nikhil/Marissa): Separate “Get set up” from “First production launch” to keep TTFS short.
- 2026-01-22 (Design): Align step titles with Console nav labels when possible (“Usage dashboard”).
- 2026-01-27 (SDK Monica/Ibrahim): Don’t overpromise cross-SDK behavior (request IDs / typed errors) until parity is verified.

TODO / open items
- Confirm final doc URLs + UTM conventions for Console deep links (see DES-115).
- Confirm whether we use “Usage dashboard” or “Usage & billing” as the nav label in Console.
- Decide if we want any “optional” tag in UI for advanced steps (streaming/structured output) or keep them standard.
- Add localized copy considerations? (Probably no for Phase 1.)

Notes to self (Wei)
- Keep descriptions <= ~120 chars if possible. The UI feels cramped beyond that.
- Avoid mentioning exact status code (200/401/429) except in troubleshooting surfaces.
- Make sure every CTA maps to a stable landing page (Docs IA will change; avoid deep-linking into anchors unless we commit to redirects).
